title: AM-GM inequality
text: AM-GM inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: For positive x_1,...,x_n, (x_1+...+x_n)/n >= (x_1...x_n)^(1/n), with equality iff all variables are equal. Conditions: Variables are nonnegative; standard multiplicative form requires positive variables. Use when: fixed product; lower bound of a sum; symmetric positive variables; product-to-sum conversion. Strategy: Normalize if useful, group positive terms, then apply AM-GM with weights matching target exponents. Common errors: Applying to negative quantities; Ignoring equality conditions.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality
text: Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: (sum a_i b_i)^2 <= (sum a_i^2)(sum b_i^2). Engel form: sum x_i^2/y_i >= (sum x_i)^2/(sum y_i) for y_i>0. Conditions: Real sequences; denominators in Engel form must be positive. Use when: sum of squares; fractional inequalities; quadratic forms; bounding sums of ratios. Strategy: Choose vectors or rewrite fractions so the denominator sum becomes controllable. Common errors: Using Engel form with nonpositive denominator; Losing equality-case information.

title: Hölder inequality
text: Hölder inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: A common form is (sum a_i^3)(sum b_i^3)(sum c_i^3) >= (sum a_i b_i c_i)^3. Conditions: Usual real nonnegative form for olympiad use. Use when: cubic powers; products of three sums; fraction inequalities with powers. Strategy: Match factors so the target expression becomes the mixed product in Hölder. Common errors: Mismatched exponents; Applying without checking nonnegativity in the chosen form.

title: Jensen inequality
text: Jensen inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: For convex f, f(sum w_i x_i) <= sum w_i f(x_i). Reverse for concave f. Conditions: Function convex on an interval containing all inputs; weights nonnegative and sum to 1. Use when: convex functions; logarithms; trigonometric inequalities; symmetric averages. Strategy: Check the second derivative and domain before invoking Jensen. Common errors: Wrong convexity interval; Wrong inequality direction; Unnormalized weights.

title: Chebyshev sum inequality
text: Chebyshev sum inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: For similarly sorted sequences, average(a_i b_i) >= average(a_i) average(b_i). Conditions: Two similarly sorted real sequences. Use when: ordered variables; correlated sums; symmetric inequalities. Strategy: Sort or establish monotonic pairing explicitly. Common errors: Sequences not similarly sorted.

title: Rearrangement inequality
text: Rearrangement inequality. Domain: algebra. Topic: inequality. Statement: The sum of pairwise products is maximal when similarly ordered and minimal when oppositely ordered. Conditions: Two real sequences sorted in the same/opposite order. Use when: permutation sums; ordered variables; assignment of coefficients. Strategy: Order both sequences, then compare the target pairing with extremal pairings. Common errors: Using without a proven ordering.

title: Vieta formulas
text: Vieta formulas. Domain: algebra. Topic: polynomials. Statement: For a monic polynomial x^n + a_{n-1}x^{n-1}+...+a_0, elementary symmetric sums of roots equal signed coefficients. Conditions: Polynomial roots counted with multiplicity. Use when: root sums/products; integer roots; symmetric expressions in roots. Strategy: Translate root constraints into symmetric sums before solving. Common errors: Sign mistakes; Ignoring multiplicity.

title: Quadratic discriminant
text: Quadratic discriminant. Domain: algebra. Topic: polynomials. Statement: Real roots exist iff Delta=b^2-4ac >= 0; repeated root iff Delta=0. Conditions: Quadratic ax^2+bx+c with a != 0. Use when: existence of real parameter; tangency; quadratic optimization. Strategy: Convert existence into a discriminant constraint. Common errors: Forgetting leading coefficient nonzero.

title: uvw reduction heuristic
text: uvw reduction heuristic. Domain: algebra. Topic: symmetric_inequality. Statement: Many symmetric 3-variable inequalities can be expressed in u=a+b+c, v^2=ab+bc+ca, w^3=abc; extremality often reduces to two equal variables. Conditions: Symmetric polynomial/rational inequality in three variables, typically homogeneous. Use when: three-variable symmetric homogeneous inequality; polynomial inequality. Strategy: First verify symmetry/homogeneity; express in elementary symmetric quantities and justify reduction. Common errors: Treating the two-equal reduction as universally automatic without justification.

title: Euclidean algorithm
text: Euclidean algorithm. Domain: number_theory. Topic: gcd. Statement: gcd(a,b)=gcd(b,a mod b); repeated division computes gcd. Conditions: Integers, not both zero. Use when: gcd; linear combinations; coprimality. Strategy: Reduce large gcd expressions using gcd(a,b)=gcd(a,b-ka). Common errors: Modulo sign confusion.

title: Bézout identity
text: Bézout identity. Domain: number_theory. Topic: gcd. Statement: There exist integers x,y with ax+by=gcd(a,b). Conditions: Integers a,b, not both zero. Use when: linear Diophantine equations; modular inverses; coprimality. Strategy: Use extended Euclid to construct coefficients. Common errors: Assuming ax+by=1 when gcd(a,b) != 1.

title: Euclid's lemma
text: Euclid's lemma. Domain: number_theory. Topic: divisibility. Statement: If prime p divides ab, then p divides a or p divides b. Conditions: p prime. Use when: prime divisibility; factor arguments; unique factorization. Strategy: Factor the expression and use primality at the critical step. Common errors: Replacing prime p with arbitrary composite divisor.

title: Fermat's little theorem
text: Fermat's little theorem. Domain: number_theory. Topic: modular_arithmetic. Statement: a^p ≡ a (mod p); if p does not divide a then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p). Conditions: p prime; for multiplicative form gcd(a,p)=1. Use when: large exponent modulo prime; periodicity. Strategy: Reduce exponents modulo p-1 only after checking coprimality. Common errors: Using p-1 exponent when p divides a.

title: Euler theorem
text: Euler theorem. Domain: number_theory. Topic: modular_arithmetic. Statement: a^phi(n) ≡ 1 (mod n). Conditions: gcd(a,n)=1. Use when: large exponent modulo composite; multiplicative order. Strategy: Factor n, compute phi(n), and reduce exponent when coprime. Common errors: Ignoring gcd(a,n)=1.

title: Chinese remainder theorem
text: Chinese remainder theorem. Domain: number_theory. Topic: congruences. Statement: A compatible system x≡a_i mod n_i with pairwise coprime n_i has a unique solution modulo product n_i. Conditions: Moduli pairwise coprime in the standard simple form. Use when: simultaneous congruences; split composite modulus. Strategy: Solve congruences locally then reconstruct. Common errors: Assuming uniqueness modulo product when moduli are not coprime.

title: Lifting the Exponent (LTE)
text: Lifting the Exponent (LTE). Domain: number_theory. Topic: valuation. Statement: For odd prime p with p|x-y and p∤xy, v_p(x^n-y^n)=v_p(x-y)+v_p(n). Special variants apply to sums and p=2. Conditions: Prime p divides x-y, p does not divide xy; formulas depend on p and parity. Use when: x^n-y^n divisibility; p-adic valuation; high powers. Strategy: Before LTE, explicitly verify prime, divisibility, coprimality, and parity conditions. Common errors: Using odd-prime formula for p=2; Missing p|x-y; Using when p divides xy.

title: Legendre formula
text: Legendre formula. Domain: number_theory. Topic: valuation. Statement: v_p(n!) = floor(n/p)+floor(n/p^2)+... . Conditions: p prime, n positive integer. Use when: factorial divisibility; trailing prime powers; binomial valuations. Strategy: Sum floors until p^k>n. Common errors: Stopping sum too early/late.

title: Wilson theorem
text: Wilson theorem. Domain: number_theory. Topic: modular_arithmetic. Statement: p is prime iff (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p). Conditions: p>1 integer. Use when: factorial modulo prime; prime characterization. Strategy: Pair modular inverses among nonzero residues. Common errors: Using as efficient primality test in computation.

title: Residue pigeonhole principle
text: Residue pigeonhole principle. Domain: number_theory. Topic: residues. Statement: Among sufficiently many integers, two share a residue modulo m; differences then are divisible by m. Conditions: Finite residue classes. Use when: divisible differences; subset sums; partial sums. Strategy: Map objects to residues and count classes carefully. Common errors: Incorrect number of boxes/classes.

title: Infinite descent
text: Infinite descent. Domain: number_theory. Topic: proof_method. Statement: A positive-integer counterexample cannot exist if every counterexample yields a strictly smaller positive counterexample. Conditions: Assume a minimal positive counterexample and construct a smaller one. Use when: Diophantine impossibility; Pythagorean-style arguments. Strategy: Define the minimal measure before constructing the descent. Common errors: No well-founded decreasing quantity.

title: Pigeonhole principle
text: Pigeonhole principle. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: counting. Statement: Some box contains at least ceil(N/k) objects. Conditions: N objects placed into k boxes. Use when: existence; residue classes; geometric partitioning; equal-value collisions. Strategy: The main work is designing boxes that make a collision useful. Common errors: Wrong choice of boxes.

title: Inclusion-exclusion principle
text: Inclusion-exclusion principle. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: counting. Statement: |A∪B|=|A|+|B|-|A∩B|, generalized by alternating sums over intersections. Conditions: Finite sets/events. Use when: forbidden properties; surjections; derangements; union counting. Strategy: Define bad-property sets explicitly and enumerate intersections. Common errors: Missing higher-order intersections; Sign mistakes.

title: Double counting
text: Double counting. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: counting. Statement: Count the same finite set in two different ways to derive an identity or inequality. Conditions: Finite set of incidences/pairs. Use when: graph degrees; incidence geometry; binomial identities. Strategy: Name the counted set before counting it two ways. Common errors: Counting different underlying sets on the two sides.

title: Extremal principle
text: Extremal principle. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: proof_method. Statement: Choose an object maximizing/minimizing a useful quantity and exploit extremality. Conditions: Finite or well-ordered candidate set. Use when: graphs; geometry-combinatorics; set systems; processes. Strategy: Choose a measure linked directly to the contradiction or desired structure. Common errors: Extremal object exists but chosen measure gives no leverage.

title: Invariant method
text: Invariant method. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: processes. Statement: If an invariant differs between initial and target states, the target is unreachable. Conditions: A repeated operation preserves a quantity/property. Use when: games; coloring moves; coin operations; parity processes. Strategy: Test parity, residue, coloring, weighted sums, and graph components. Common errors: Claiming invariance without checking every legal move.

title: Monovariant method
text: Monovariant method. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: processes. Statement: A strictly decreasing/increasing bounded measure proves termination or forbids cycles. Conditions: A quantity strictly moves in one direction and is bounded/well-founded. Use when: algorithms; games; iterative transformations. Strategy: Find an integer-valued energy or lexicographic measure. Common errors: Measure is not strictly monotone for every move.

title: Ramsey principle
text: Ramsey principle. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: graphs. Statement: Sufficiently large structures contain a homogeneous substructure; e.g. every 2-coloring of edges of K6 has a monochromatic triangle. Conditions: Finite complete graph/coloring setting. Use when: friend/stranger problems; edge colorings; homogeneous subsets. Strategy: Use degree pigeonhole followed by local case analysis for small Ramsey problems. Common errors: Using a Ramsey number without proof/allowed citation.

title: Hall marriage theorem
text: Hall marriage theorem. Domain: combinatorics. Topic: matching. Statement: A matching covering every vertex of left part exists iff every subset S of left vertices has |N(S)|>=|S|. Conditions: Finite bipartite graph. Use when: systems of distinct representatives; assignment; matching. Strategy: Translate choices to a bipartite graph, then verify Hall condition for arbitrary subsets. Common errors: Checking only singleton neighborhoods.

title: Triangle similarity
text: Triangle similarity. Domain: geometry. Topic: similarity. Statement: Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding sides. Conditions: AA, SAS proportional, or SSS proportional criteria. Use when: ratio chasing; cyclic configurations; altitudes; angle bisectors. Strategy: Write correspondence order explicitly before taking ratios. Common errors: Mismatching corresponding vertices.

title: Ceva theorem
text: Ceva theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: concurrency. Statement: AD, BE, CF are concurrent iff (BD/DC)(CE/EA)(AF/FB)=1 in the standard positive interior case. Conditions: Triangle ABC with D,E,F on opposite sides or extensions; directed form handles extensions. Use when: concurrency of cevians; ratio geometry. Strategy: Choose a consistent cyclic orientation of the three ratios. Common errors: Ignoring directed lengths for extensions; Wrong ratio orientation.

title: Menelaus theorem
text: Menelaus theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: collinearity. Statement: D,E,F are collinear iff the product of three directed side ratios equals -1 (or 1 in unsigned convention with one external point). Conditions: Triangle and three points on sides/extensions; directed lengths recommended. Use when: collinearity; ratio chasing. Strategy: Fix directed-segment convention before multiplying ratios. Common errors: Sign convention confusion.

title: Power of a point
text: Power of a point. Domain: geometry. Topic: circle. Statement: For secant PAB, power(P)=PA·PB; for tangent PT, power(P)=PT^2. Conditions: Point P and circle; secants/tangents interpreted with directed lengths as needed. Use when: circle intersections; tangency; radical axis; length products. Strategy: Identify one point with two secants/tangents and equate powers. Common errors: Using wrong intersection order; Unsigned lengths in external/internal cases.

title: Radical axis theorem
text: Radical axis theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: circle. Statement: Points with equal powers to two circles lie on a line, the radical axis; three pairwise radical axes are concurrent unless parallel. Conditions: Two nonconcentric circles. Use when: multiple circles; hidden collinearity; coaxality. Strategy: Translate equal products into equal powers. Common errors: Confusing radical axis with line of centers.

title: Inscribed angle theorem
text: Inscribed angle theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: circle. Statement: An inscribed angle equals half the measure of its intercepted arc; equal chords subtend equal angles. Conditions: Angles subtend arcs/chords in a circle. Use when: cyclic quadrilateral; angle chasing; equal chord arguments. Strategy: Track which chord each angle subtends. Common errors: Using opposite arcs incorrectly.

title: Ptolemy theorem
text: Ptolemy theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: circle. Statement: AC·BD = AB·CD + BC·AD. Conditions: Cyclic quadrilateral ABCD. Use when: cyclic quadrilateral lengths; diagonals; trigonometric identities. Strategy: First prove cyclicity, then identify diagonal and opposite-side products. Common errors: Applying to noncyclic quadrilateral.

title: Law of sines
text: Law of sines. Domain: geometry. Topic: triangle. Statement: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R. Conditions: Nondegenerate triangle. Use when: circumradius; side-angle conversion; trigonometric geometry. Strategy: Use when angle information is cleaner than side ratios. Common errors: Mismatching side and opposite angle.

title: Law of cosines
text: Law of cosines. Domain: geometry. Topic: triangle. Statement: c^2=a^2+b^2-2ab cos C. Conditions: Nondegenerate triangle. Use when: side-angle conversion; median/vector-like geometry. Strategy: Use to eliminate an angle or convert quadratic length relations. Common errors: Wrong opposite side/angle.

title: Stewart theorem
text: Stewart theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: cevian. Statement: b^2 m + c^2 n = (m+n)(d^2+mn), with b=CA and c=AB. Conditions: Triangle ABC, point D on BC; denote BD=m, DC=n, BC=m+n, AD=d. Use when: cevian length; median; angle bisector. Strategy: Draw labels explicitly before substitution. Common errors: Swapping b,c relative to m,n.

title: Angle bisector theorem
text: Angle bisector theorem. Domain: geometry. Topic: cevian. Statement: BD/DC = AB/AC. Conditions: AD bisects angle A in triangle ABC, D on BC. Use when: side ratios; incenter; bisectors. Strategy: Turn angle-bisector information into a side ratio early. Common errors: Using converse without verifying ratio.

title: Spiral similarity
text: Spiral similarity. Domain: geometry. Topic: transformation. Statement: A direct spiral similarity maps one segment to another via rotation+dilation; its center often lies at intersection of circumcircles/angle loci. Conditions: Two oriented segments or similar triangles with a common similarity center. Use when: two segments with equal subtended angles; cyclic quadrilaterals; Miquel-style configurations. Strategy: Search for equal oriented angles showing two triangles are directly similar. Common errors: Asserting a spiral center without proving angle/ratio correspondence.

title: Homogenization
text: Homogenization. Domain: general. Topic: strategy. Statement: Introduce an appropriate scale/constraint so all terms have the same degree. Conditions: Problem has a normalization or expressions of mixed degree. Use when: inequalities; projective ratio problems; fixed sum/product. Strategy: Identify scaling behavior and use a legitimate normalization. Common errors: Changing the feasible set incorrectly.

title: Substitution
text: Substitution. Domain: general. Topic: strategy. Statement: Replace variables by new variables that encode positivity, product, sum, or geometric structure. Conditions: A constraint suggests parametrization. Use when: abc=1; positive variables; Pythagorean relations; ratio constraints. Strategy: State why every admissible original configuration is represented. Common errors: Substitution not surjective onto original feasible set.

title: Proof by contradiction
text: Proof by contradiction. Domain: general. Topic: proof_method. Statement: Assume the desired statement is false and derive a contradiction with a hypothesis or established fact. Conditions: Negation of target yields exploitable structure. Use when: irrationality; uniqueness; extremal impossibility. Strategy: Write the exact negation, especially for quantified statements. Common errors: Deriving only an unlikely statement, not a logical contradiction.

title: Mathematical induction
text: Mathematical induction. Domain: general. Topic: proof_method. Statement: Prove P(n0), then P(k)->P(k+1) to obtain P(n) for all n>=n0. Conditions: Statement indexed by natural numbers; base case and inductive implication available. Use when: recurrences; divisibility sequences; combinatorial identities. Strategy: Consider strengthening the induction hypothesis if the step stalls. Common errors: Induction hypothesis stronger/weaker than needed; Missing base cases.

title: Symmetry exploitation
text: Symmetry exploitation. Domain: general. Topic: strategy. Statement: Symmetry can reduce cases, motivate equal-variable extremals, or suggest symmetric invariants. Conditions: Problem invariant under variable/object permutations. Use when: symmetric inequalities; geometry with interchangeable vertices; counting. Strategy: Verify invariance before imposing WLOG order. Common errors: Assuming WLOG an ordering when the expression is not fully symmetric.

title: positive variables with fixed product; bound a sum
text: Strategy pattern: positive variables with fixed product; bound a sum. Domain: algebra. Signals: positive; product fixed; lower bound sum. Suggested approaches: AM-GM; normalization; uvw if symmetric 3-variable. Avoid: random expansion.

title: symmetric homogeneous inequality in three variables
text: Strategy pattern: symmetric homogeneous inequality in three variables. Domain: algebra. Signals: symmetric; homogeneous; three variables. Suggested approaches: uvw; pqr; two-equal-variable extremal after justification; AM-GM/Cauchy. Avoid: assuming a=b without justification.

title: divisibility of a^n-b^n by prime powers
text: Strategy pattern: divisibility of a^n-b^n by prime powers. Domain: number_theory. Signals: difference of powers; valuation; prime power divisibility. Suggested approaches: LTE; factorization; multiplicative order. Avoid: LTE without checking conditions.

title: large exponent modulo m
text: Strategy pattern: large exponent modulo m. Domain: number_theory. Signals: large exponent; modulo. Suggested approaches: Euler/Fermat; CRT; multiplicative order. Avoid: reducing exponent mod phi(m) without coprimality.

title: find divisible subset/consecutive sum
text: Strategy pattern: find divisible subset/consecutive sum. Domain: combinatorics. Signals: partial sums; divisibility; existence. Suggested approaches: pigeonhole on residues; zero residue case. Avoid: forgetting equal-residue difference.

title: repeated legal moves; reachability or termination
text: Strategy pattern: repeated legal moves; reachability or termination. Domain: combinatorics. Signals: operation; moves; state; reach. Suggested approaches: invariant; monovariant; parity; coloring. Avoid: checking only sample moves.

title: products of segment lengths around circles/secants
text: Strategy pattern: products of segment lengths around circles/secants. Domain: geometry. Signals: circle; secant; tangent; product of lengths. Suggested approaches: power of a point; radical axis. Avoid: Ptolemy without cyclic quadrilateral.

title: three cevians concurrent
text: Strategy pattern: three cevians concurrent. Domain: geometry. Signals: triangle; three cevians; concurrent. Suggested approaches: Ceva; mass points; trigonometric Ceva. Avoid: ratio orientation mistakes.

title: three points on sides/extensions are collinear
text: Strategy pattern: three points on sides/extensions are collinear. Domain: geometry. Signals: triangle; collinear; side points. Suggested approaches: Menelaus; directed lengths. Avoid: sign convention ambiguity.

title: two segment pairs with equal oriented angles
text: Strategy pattern: two segment pairs with equal oriented angles. Domain: geometry. Signals: equal angles; two segments; cyclic. Suggested approaches: spiral similarity; cyclic quadrilateral; similar triangles. Avoid: declaring similarity center without proof.

title: Completely additive arithmetic functions
text: If g(ab)=g(a)+g(b) on positive integers, then g is determined by its values on primes: for n=product p^e, g(n)=sum e*g(p). Integer-valued or positive-valued constraints become linear constraints on the prime weights. Strategy: factor the target and every bounded input that can impose a tight constraint. Common errors: claiming the only solutions are constant or c log n; forgetting arbitrary prime weights.

title: Conjugate a binary operation to multiplication or addition
text: For a functional equation involving a repeated binary expression, seek a simple shift/scale h with h(x operation y)=h(x)h(y) or h(x)+h(y). Factor expressions before iterating substitutions. After conjugacy, characterize the resulting homomorphism structurally rather than by guessing a closed form. Common errors: using a transformed domain that omits necessary inputs; assuming continuity when the domain is integers.

title: Extremal tiling needs both a bound and a realizable construction
text: For partitions or tilings with distinct rectangle invariants, separate the proof into a numerical upper bound and a geometric construction attaining it. Minimizing each rectangle's area independently for a given perimeter can give a bound, but does not prove those rectangles tile the board. Track boundary/grid constraints and realizability explicitly.

title: Binary-weighted rounds encode histories uniquely
text: When round weights are distinct powers of two, a final score uniquely encodes the set of rounds won. In equal-state pairing processes, group participants by identical history/state, derive the recursive block sizes, then count possible relative orderings. For divisibility of the count, compute prime valuations only after deriving the exact counting formula.

title: Coordinate reduction for cyclic incidence with integer sides
text: For geometry problems mixing cyclic quadrilaterals, collinearity, equal lengths, and an integer-side extremum, first derive an exact algebraic condition using power of a point, radical axis, directed ratios, or coordinates. Then search integer side triples only after the condition is derived. Common error: guessing familiar triples and retrofitting the geometry.
